idea.title: A shared footer needs a reserved visual band
idea.summary: The footer existed in the DOM, but flexible slide content could consume its visual space. Reserving and layering a shared footer band made the handle reliable in every exported composition.

context.goal: Make the shared personal-carousel footer visible in all seven layouts.
context.situation: Some exported slides appeared to lose the handle despite rendering the shared Footer component.
context.problem: The footer relied on remaining flex space after variable content regions.
context.investigation: Computed layout showed the footer node existed; the composition needed a reserved area instead of a flow-dependent one.
context.decision: Position the shared personal footer in its own safe band and reserve that band from layout content.
context.implementation: Adjusted the personal-frame CSS and added export checks for footer text bounds on all seven slides.
context.result: The seven PNG exports retained the handle within the safe area while short and longer content still avoided overflow.

learning_points: DOM presence does not prove a repeated visual element is readable in a rendered export.
Shared fixed information needs reserved spatial ownership when sibling content can grow.
Visual tests should assert bounds and inspect the resulting PNGs.
story_points: The first instinct could have been to add another footer per layout.
The shared layout layer already owned the correct component, so the fix stayed in one CSS rule.
The result held across Studio preview, Studio export, and the Playwright route.
possible_angles: Why a footer can exist in the DOM and still disappear in an exported image.
How to give repeated content a real safe area in variable layouts.

notes: No post substance or renderer data contracts were changed.
